SsoPage.samlOkta: Okta: create a SAML 2.0 app; Single sign-on URL = ACS URL, Audience URI = Entity ID, Name ID format EmailAddress; add a group attribute statement (e.g. groups, filter “Matches regex .*”); copy the IdP metadata URL's XML here.
SsoPage.samlEntra: Entra ID: Enterprise applications → New → Non-gallery, Single sign-on → SAML; Identifier = Entity ID, Reply URL = ACS URL; add a group claim; download “Federation Metadata XML” and paste it here. Groups arrive as object IDs unless you emit names.
SsoPage.samlAdfs: ADFS: add a relying party trust from the SP metadata URL; claim rules: E-Mail-Address → Name ID (email format) and Token-Groups → groups; paste https://<adfs>/FederationMetadata/2007-06/FederationMetadata.xml here.

ProvisioningPage.description: Let your identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin …) create, update and remove members over SCIM 2.0. Groups map to roles with the group → role mapping in Single sign-on.
ProvisioningPage.howItWorks: Deactivating or deleting a user at the IdP removes their membership, revokes their API keys in this workspace and ends the sessions they started through this workspace’s single sign-on. They can’t rejoin through SSO until the IdP reactivates them. Owners are never demoted, and the last owner is never removed.

OrgProvisioning.title: Provisioning
OrgProvisioning.description: Turn identity-provider groups into access: organization admins and roles in the organization’s workspaces.
OrgProvisioning.rulesHelp: Members of a group get the role in the workspace; the most permissive rule wins. Memberships granted by rules follow them and are removed when no rule matches; memberships people were invited to are left alone. Groups come from SCIM when it is on, otherwise from the single sign-on assertion. Workspaces with their own SSO (or SCIM) are left to it.
OrgProvisioning.rules: Rules, one per line: group = workspace:role
OrgProvisioning.adminGroups: Organization admin groups (one per line); the IdP never removes an admin
OrgProvisioning.scimHowItWorks: Users created over SCIM join the organization; group rules assign their workspaces. Deactivating or deleting a user removes them from the organization and its workspaces, revokes their API keys there and ends the sessions they started through the organization’s single sign-on. The last organization admin and each workspace’s last owner are kept.
